entry.title: Show HN: MapDex - A Social Map for Travelers (Source: hnrss.org | Category: Hacker News)
entry.summary: MapDex is a social map for travelers. Users can track places they've visited, save destinations to their bucket list, and explore maps from friends and other travelers. One thing I felt was missing from existing products was meaningful ranking. Instead of relying on a traditional 5-star system where ratings tend to become inflated, MapDex lets users rank destinations against others within the same category. Cities are ranked against cities, beaches against beaches, countries against countries, and so on. The goal is to create a more useful way to discover places through people you trust while building a visual record of where you've been and where you want to go next. The app is currently live on iOS and Android. I'd love feedback on the product, ranking system, positioning, and growth strategy. iOS: https://apps.apple.com/us/app/mapdex/id6762475774 Android: https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.mapdex.app Comments URL: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=48616623 Points: 1 # Comments: 0

entry.title: Ask HN: Favorite Aspects of Cocoa/NeXTSTEP? (Source: hnrss.org | Category: Hacker News)
entry.summary: What's your favorite parts of Cocoa? Personally I've been a Mac OS X fan for a long time. Before that Étoilé was a favorite. Is there anything in the programming side or design of NextSTEP and later Cocoa that lent itself to so many beautiful Mac OS X apps being made? I've been working on an implementation of OpenStep and Cocoa. The first piece was dynamic runtime methods and protocols. It made adding a view inspector trivial! However were dynamic/runtime methods the only magic of Cocoa? It feels like we've lost some of the art of desktop apps. Comments URL: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=48616604 Points: 1 # Comments: 0

entry.title: Show HN: StartupWiki - A Free Alternative to Crunchbase (Source: hnrss.org | Category: Hacker News)
entry.summary: I've been building StartupWiki, a free startup database designed to make it easier to discover and research companies. The original motivation was frustration with how difficult it can be to find information on early-stage startups. Most databases need accounts, or subscriptions, ro just feel too cluttered. I wanted a website that felt like Wikipedia, no accounts, no subscriptions, no weird metrics, just go in, the info is on the page. The project is still very early, but currently includes: Startup profiles Search and filtering Company categorization Public API (in progress) I'm especially interested in feedback on: What information you look for when researching startups Features missing from existing startup databases API use cases I'd love to hear feedback. Comments URL: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=48610224 Points: 192 # Comments: 59
